inputs.text: Mahama’s talk of law, culture, and “collective societal agreement” is how they manufacture consent and make institutional control look inevitable. And that clipped oath—“I took an oath to uphold [...]”—is no harmless edit: it hides what the duty actually serves. They’re asking people to trust the script while keeping its beneficiaries out of view.

output.main_topic: Critical claims that Mahama’s rhetoric and an edited oath conceal institutional control and its beneficiaries
subtopics: Law, culture, and collective societal agreement
output.narrative_frame: Critical framing of rhetoric and oath editing as concealing the beneficiaries of institutional control.
opinions: The text characterizes talk of law, culture, and “collective societal agreement” as a means of manufacturing consent and making institutional control appear inevitable.
The text judges the clipped oath edit as harmful because it hides what the duty serves.
The text accuses an unspecified group of asking people to trust a script while keeping its beneficiaries out of view.
